name: F6S
requirements: Account required — everything on the site sits behind one; signup offers Google, email, and behind 'Continue another way' LinkedIn and Facebook.
Creating a company page takes just two fields — name and website — and the page publishes immediately with no review.
Outbound links are rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" — the value is the profile plus access to accelerator/deal feeds, not SEO link equity.
preparation: Company name and live website URL — the two fields that create the page.
One-line description; location and founding year.
Markets: a closed-vocabulary picker that rejects invented phrases and adds a parent category per pick — they ask for 5+.
Team members (invitable, can claim the profile), investors, decks/media, traction data.
Optional: software pricing/features section that unlocks reviews.
workflow: Add your company: name + website — page exists immediately; skip the optional team-invite screen if unneeded.
Work through the 'Complete page' editor's nine left-rail sections: Overview, Investors, Page Info, Team, Decks and Media, Product, Traction, Recommendations, Advanced — it autosaves (no save button).
Fill the markets picker with 5+ valid entries; a profile-strength meter pushes completeness.
Keep the page current — complete profiles rank better on F6S's startup/company collection pages.
watchFor: No anonymous submission exists — the account is the whole gate.
Links are nofollow — don't count this as a backlink source.
Autosave editor with no save button — trust it, but verify fields persisted.
Markets picker uses a closed vocabulary — invented phrases get rejected.
Premium plans exist for enhanced features/deal access — not needed for a basic profile.
Homepage returned HTTP 405 to a plain fetcher — expect a real browser session to be necessary.
countsAsLive: A public company page at f6s.com/company/<slug> (or /p/) reachable while logged out, populated via the nine-section editor.
unknowns: Whether profile completeness affects any approval (reported: no review at all).
